clue.text: Obstinate duchess distressed when divorced from husband

indicators.note: something distressed is knocked out of shape, so the letters are jumbled
being divorced from something means parting company with it, so one letter is taken away

blocks.note: taken as written
H is the standard abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A stubborn duchess is upset by her divorce from her husband.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the H out of DUCHESS first, then rearrange the remaining six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Cussed is an informal word for stubborn and awkward, unwilling to cooperate with others.

clue.text: Old dispute affected Labour’s leader over symbolic field strength?

indicators.note: a leader is the front of something, so only its opening letter is wanted here
in a down clue, over means placed above, so this part comes earlier in the entry

blocks.note: camp means exaggerated, theatrical, affected in manner
the first letter of Labour
E is the physics symbol for electric field strength

explanation.surface: A political quarrel about Labour's leader and the strength of his support in some field.
explanation.walkthrough: CAMPLE is an obsolete verb meaning to wrangle; physics uses E as the symbol for electric field strength.
explanation.definitionFit: Cample is an archaic verb in Chambers meaning to argue or wrangle, matching an old word for dispute.

clue.text: Plonker dismissing new upper-class language

indicators.note: dismissing someone sends them away, so a letter is dropped from the word

blocks.note: nurd is a variant spelling of nerd, a foolish or dull person
N is the abbreviation for new
U is the old label for upper-class usage

explanation.surface: A posh idiot drops some new piece of upper-class slang.
explanation.walkthrough: A plonker is British slang for a fool; NURD is Chambers' variant of nerd, and it loses its N.
explanation.definitionFit: Urdu is an Indo-Aryan language, official in Pakistan and widely spoken in India.

clue.text: Fabulous beast that is right to be comparatively short

blocks.note: the snark is the imaginary creature of Lewis Carroll's poem
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A mythical creature is described as being on the stubby side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' is meant as short-tempered, not small, which the fabulous-beast picture hides.
explanation.definitionFit: Snarky means irritable or sharp-tongued, so snarkier is the comparative of being curt with people.

clue.text: This would soak up cans of beer I spilt over time

indicators.note: spilt contents land in a mess, so the letters are scattered into a new order
in a down clue, over means placed above, so the jumbled part sits on top

blocks.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone mopping up the beer they knocked over, given enough time.
explanation.definitionFit: A sorbefacient is a medical agent that promotes absorption, something whose job is to take in fluid.

clue.text: Under British Left this gas could make you a sweetie-wife

indicators.note: this word would sit below two letters to form a longer one, so it is that word minus its opening pair
says the longer word is what you would get by adding, so the entry is what remains once those additions go

blocks.note: a sweetie-wife is a Scots gossip, and so is a blether
B is the abbreviation for British
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A gas so potent it might turn you into a chatterbox.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits in the middle: put B and L on top of ETHER and you get BLETHER, Scots for a gossip, as is sweetie-wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Ether is a volatile anaesthetic vapour, so it is loosely a gas used by doctors.

clue.text: Victor behind one in grip of strong hint

indicators.note: behind means coming after, so the first item follows the second
being held in someone's grip means being enclosed by them

blocks.note: sour as in strong-tasting or sharp
a means one
Victor is V in the radio alphabet

explanation.walkthrough: A V sits inside S...OUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A savour is a faint taste or trace of something, so it can mean a hint or suggestion.

clue.text: Dips of a similar sort in goss that’s upsetting

indicators.note: upsetting means knocking over and disarranging, so the letters change order
one part goes inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
akin means related, of the same kind

explanation.walkthrough: Goss is short for gossip; jumble it to SOGS and put AKIN inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A soaking is an immersion in liquid, so soakings are plural noun synonyms for dips.

clue.text: Trailers carrying current benefits

clue.text: Early atomic idea is farcically extrovert and, oh, unknown

clue.text: Like wee hot iron in service

taken as written

blocks.note: taken as written

clue.text: Jack leans here to face banter

clue.text: Supply person with bucket for quarried material

clue.text: Excess food storage? Fine to be ripped off

clue.text: Spoke about getting accepted annoyed apostate

clue.text: Frame longshoremen concealing shared issue

clue.text: Check one on run? OK, go on recklessly

clue.text: Cases of pedestrians bagging apparently nothing

blocks.note: peds is short for pedestrians

clue.text: Quietly claim university raised result

clue.text: Complex NT tongue not learned?

blocks.note: taken as written

clue.text: Called for northern adult section to disappear
